title: Metatranscriptomic Screening for Genes of Interest
author: Helena Pound
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.7vyhn7w
materials: Export FinalCandidatesProtein sequence list as a .fasta file

steps.title: Create Reference Database
steps.instruction: Create a database from the list of genes of interest (reference.fasta) using protein sequences in the command line window.

substeps.instruction: Run: makeblastdb -dbtype prot -in reference.fasta -parse_seqids

steps.title: Blast Assembly Against Reference
steps.instruction: Blast the assembly against the created reference database to produce a list of contigs (candidates) in a file named final.txt.

substeps.instruction: Run: blastx -query assembly.fasta -db reference.fasta -out final.txt -outfmt "6 qseqid sseqid pident length mismatch gapopen qstart qend sstart send evalue bitscore qframe" -e-value 1E-10

steps.title: Trim Candidate Contigs
steps.instruction: Trim candidate contigs to the exact length of the reference gene based on the start and finish locations of the blast alignment using a custom python script.

substeps.instruction: Ensure the .txt file contains all columns listed in the blast output format
Run the python script to trim sequences (if a contig hits multiple reference sequences, use the lowest start and highest end point)

steps.title: Process and Filter Sequences in CLC Workbench
steps.instruction: Convert the trimmed data and filter by length using CLC Workbench.

substeps.instruction: Open the .txt file in Microsoft Excel and save it as a .csv file
Import the .csv file into CLC Workbench as 'sequences in .csv format'
Sort sequences by length and delete those smaller than 150 nucleic acids (or based on personal preference)
Export the sequence list as a .fasta file and a .csv file (e.g., trimmed.fasta and trimmed.csv)

steps.title: Perform Diamond Blastx Quality Control
steps.instruction: Use Diamond blastx against the NCBI non-redundant database to identify and remove non-viral sequences.

substeps.instruction: Download the NCBI non-redundant database in .fasta format and rename to nonredundant.fasta
Create diamond database: diamond makedb --in non-redundant.fasta -d non-redundant
Run blast: diamond blastx -d nonredundant -q trimmed.fasta -o candidates.txt -f 6 qseqid sseqid pident length mismatch gapopen qstart qend sstart send evalue bitscore qframe stitle -k 1

steps.title: Filter for Viral Sequences
steps.instruction: Filter the candidates to retain only those of viral origin.

substeps.instruction: Open candidates.txt and trimmed.csv in Excel
Copy sequences from trimmed.csv to a new column in candidates.txt, ensuring sequence names match
Delete all rows containing sequences that are not viral in origin based on the diamond blast hits

steps.title: Organize Sequences by Query Frame
steps.instruction: Separate the viral sequences into files based on their query frames.

substeps.instruction: Create a new .csv file with 3 columns: sequence name, sequence, and query frame
Sort by query frame and create a separate .csv file for each frame (e.g., CandidatesQF+1.csv)
Import each query frame .csv file into CLC Workbench as separate sequence lists

steps.title: Generate Final Nucleic Acid and Protein Lists
steps.instruction: Combine the filtered sequences and translate them into protein sequences.

substeps.instruction: Create a new sequence list combining all query frame sequence lists and rename as 'FinalCandidatesNucleicAcid'
Translate each individual query frame sequence list to protein based on the specific query frame
Create a new sequence list combining all resulting protein sequences and rename as 'FinalCandidatesProtein'
